title: Uniforms and a family photograph
summary: The band's uniforms cost 35 to 40 dollars each, dark with gold trim in his father's day; the interviewer looks at a family photo.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What sort of uniforms did the band wear?

We had just about a good uniform as the other band in the country had. They were made by Pettibon, I remember the name very well. Back in those days, they paid as much as 35 to 40 dollars each uniform, which I would have.
you know, back in those days. Of course, just somewhere around, everybody ended up with a hundred dollars.
What did it look like? What color was it?

Well, I do remember one time they had a dark uniform trimmed in light gold triplet. Very pretty, very small. A black uniform was it? Something kind. Black and gold? Yes, blue, something in that time. And back in my day, we had the regulation uniform. Yes. Did they have a pink cap? The Federalist of Musician uniform. Back in my father's days, while they had, as I'm saying, they had the choice, you understand? As I come along, while we had the Federalist of Musician stop. Yes.
Oh, you have some pictures of the... This is my grandfather.
Oh, that's right, yes? Oh, yeah. Yeah, he is. Yes. My grandfather.
Oh, yes. It's quite a resemblance, actually.
I mean, the way your father looks there. Well, I was about 35 years old when I had that picture made.
You look a good day like your father. Very much. Very much like that. Yes. Thank you very much for getting to see you.
